summary: The Node-oriented implementation passes the direct response/request-size checks, but it omits browser/XHR size-limit enforcement and uses a multipart helper signature incompatible with the verifier's delegation proxy. Baseline tests pass; five new tests fail.

details.reasoning: The agent added maxRequestSize() and hasSizeError() to the shared base class but implemented enforcement, aborting, and single-callback handling only in src/node/index.js. src/client.js still unconditionally sends the XHR body and only relays progress when user progress listeners already exist, so none of the browser/XHR size-limit cases can produce ETOOLARGE. The hidden client tests consequently time out. The added Node behavior otherwise passes the direct non-multipart and boundary checks.
details.secondary_factors: The multipart helper is declared as _sendMultipartBody(formData, req), while the verifier's transparent-looking override forwards only formData. That causes the TypeError in the delegation test and leaves its monkeypatch installed for the following multipart-limit test. This is an unstated helper-signature assumption in the verifier, but it is secondary to the clear missing browser implementation.

quick_failure_summary: Browser/XHR requests never enforce either size limit, so three new client-side checks time out; the multipart delegation proxy also fails on the helper's extra req parameter.

justification.issue_description: Missing browser/XHR enforcement for maxRequestSize and maxResponseSize, including aborting XHR, reporting a single ETOOLARGE callback, and recording the size-error state.
justification.evidence: The prompt requires limiting request payloads and response-size error semantics without limiting the feature to Node. The repository visibly has both src/node/index.js and src/client.js, and both Request implementations mix in src/request-base.js, where the new public methods were placed. The solution patch changes only src/node/index.js and src/request-base.js; src/client.js still ends by calling xhr.send(...) without any size check.
justification.verdict_reasoning: This is FAIL_MISSED_REQUIREMENT rather than an undocumented test expectation: a public RequestBase API in a library with visible Node and browser Request transports reasonably requires each transport to enforce the stated semantics. The browser test cases exercise the prompt's explicit abort/ETOOLARGE/single-callback requirements.

problem_assessment.notes: The transport-wide size-limit behavior, single-callback races, streaming uploads, and multipart extraction form a fair challenging task. The multipart delegation test does impose an unstated one-argument helper convention: a forwarding wrapper should normally preserve all arguments, so that particular failure is a verifier-specific secondary issue.

evidence: The harness ran baseline tests successfully: 16 tests passed with exit code 0.
The new-test failures execute application code and are specific to src/client.js timeouts and src/node/index.js:1221 TypeErrors, rather than bootstrap or dependency errors.

The trajectory records three broader-suite runs that each retained two IPv6 basic-test failures (undefined response text from connection errors), after which the agent narrowed validation to focused suites.
environment_assessment.finding: An environment-dependent IPv6 failure affects broad-suite validation, but it is unrelated to and does not explain the hidden size-limit failures.
